K_problems.problem: 25 required fields, can't be saved part-way
K_problems.why: I have at most 45 minutes. Mission and vision aren't my job, and I won't have the ERP-based KPIs or the data owner's details ready on the first sitting. If the session dies, I lose everything.

K_problems.problem: Session expires after 10 minutes of inactivity, and the form has no draft save
K_problems.why: I'll stop to check figures in the ERP or phone my analyst. When I come back, the form is wiped. That's when I close the tab.

K_problems.problem: The form asks for 'Preferred methodology*' and 'Risk appetite (1–10)*'
K_problems.why: You're the consultant, so you tell me the method and defend it. A 1–10 risk number with no definition is exactly the kind of made-up input that later turns up as a 'finding'.

K_problems.problem: 'Mission*' and 'Vision*' are required for a plant capex decision
K_problems.why: It tells me the tool runs on a generic template and isn't built around my decision. That costs it credibility straight away.

K_problems.problem: Only 3 constraints and 2 KPIs, all mandatory
K_problems.why: A second-plant decision involves IRR, payback, utilisation, the financing cost and labour availability. A fixed count either forces me to pad the form or stops me listing everything.

K_problems.problem: Jargon: EngagementSpec, EvidenceItems, M02 critical gaps, provenance class: observed, gap_01 sales_tx
K_problems.why: It's internal system language. I can't tell what the system wants, or why it wants it.

K_problems.problem: The dataset list doesn't fit my problem (cust_master, mkt_spend_ts)
K_problems.why: Marketing spend isn't what drives a plant decision. Capacity, utilisation, unit costs, the order book and capex quotes are. It looks like a canned list, and that makes me suspect the analysis is canned too.

K_problems.problem: Status shown only by red and green dots, with no legend
K_problems.why: I don't know whether red means missing, rejected or urgent. Colour on its own isn't information.

K_problems.problem: Drag-and-drop only, with no upload button
K_problems.why: It's awkward on a laptop trackpad and with files on network drives, and there's no fallback.
It doesn't say which column is wrong or what the expected format is, and it's gone before I can read it or screenshot it for my analyst.

K_problems.problem: No way to invite my analyst or give them a second account
K_problems.why: Pulling the data is my analyst's job. If only I can upload, either I do analyst work or the engagement stalls.

K_problems.problem: Only the decision owner's and data owner's emails are captured, with no roles or permissions
K_problems.why: An email address isn't access. My analyst still can't log in to upload anything.

K_problems.problem: The status screen shows only 'processing' with a spinner
K_problems.why: It gives no ETA, no stage, no sign that a human is involved, and doesn't say whether the data was accepted. For a skeptic that's the definition of a black box, and I'd assume it's stuck.

K_problems.problem: Nothing anywhere about how numbers will be sourced or checked
K_problems.why: My first question is which numbers come from my ERP and which are assumed. Nothing here promises I'll be able to tell.

K_problems.problem: No information about where the data goes or how it's handled
K_problems.why: I'm uploading confidential cost and margin data to an unnamed portal. I'd want to know about storage, retention and who sees it before uploading anything.

walkthrough: Day 0, 8 min: I type the problem in plain words: 'Should we open a second plant? The current plant runs at about 88% utilisation, there's a capex quote of roughly X, and demand is uncertain.' I answer 4 follow-up questions on the same page.

Day 0, 3 min: The next-step card says 'Confirm we understood your problem (2 min)'. In 'What we understood' I edit 'other possible causes' to add: run extra shifts or outsource instead of building. Good, it treats alternatives as real options.

Day 0, 5 min: I read the data checklist: production volumes by line, unit cost breakdown, order book and forecast, capex quotes, financing terms. Must-have and Helpful labels are clear, and the 'why we need it' line reassures me they're not pulling data for the sake of it.

Day 0, 4 min: I click 'Someone else has this → invite them' on the ERP items and invite my analyst. STUCK/SUSPICIOUS #1: it isn't clear whether my analyst gets their own account with only data rights, or sees everything, including the report before I do. I need role control.

Day 1–3 (analyst's time, mine ~0): My analyst uploads the ERP extracts. One file is rejected, but the message explains which column is wrong and shows an example, so the analyst fixes it without calling me. The next-step card flips to 'Nothing needed from you. Results expected Thu 16 Oct.'

Day 3, 2 min: I check the progress tracker (Analysis → Checking). STUCK #2: I can't see which of the uploaded files was actually used, or what the analysis assumes about things I didn't provide (demand growth, the ramp-up curve).

Day 7, 25 min: The report arrives after consultant review. The one-paragraph answer, e.g. 'Defer 12 months; add a 3rd shift first', is what I want. 'How sure are we?' per finding is good. I click [Ask a question about this] on the payback figure: 'Where does the 4.2-year payback come from?' SUSPICIOUS #3: unless every number links back to my file and row, or is explicitly labelled 'assumption: source X', I'll rebuild the model in Excel myself.

Day 8, 30 min: My analyst and I spot-check 5 numbers against the ERP. If they all trace, I download the Word version for the board pack. If even one number can't be traced, I stop trusting the whole report.
B.quote: This is the first one that tells me what it needs and why. But show me the source of every number, or a big 'ASSUMPTION' label on it, and let me change the assumptions myself, or it stays in my drawer.

walkthrough: Day 0, 10 min: I type the problem in the chat. The consultant asks questions one at a time, and after 8 messages I'm impatient because I could have written all of it in one go.
Day 0, 2 min: The summary card is fine. I click [That's right].

Day 0, 10 min: Data requests arrive one message at a time. STUCK #1: I want my analyst to handle them, but there's no obvious way to hand over a single chat message. Do I forward the whole thread to him? Then he sees everything.
Day 1–4: My analyst (if he can get access at all) uploads files mid-thread. STUCK #2: when I come back, I scroll up through 40 messages to work out what's still outstanding. There's no checklist.
Day 4, 3 min: 'I'm analysing, I'll message you when done.' SUSPICIOUS: it's the same black box as before, just with a friendly tone.

Day 8, 30 min: The report comes as a long chat message. The expandable sections help, but the assumptions are buried in prose. I ask 'Is the 18% margin from our data?' and get a conversational answer, which I can't attach to a board paper.

Day 8: I download the PDF. STUCK #3: there's no clear confidence rating per finding and no trace from each number back to its source. The chat format makes me think a language model wrote fluent text and filled the gaps with guesses.
Possible abandonment around day 4, when the thread becomes a mess and I can't tell what's been handed over.
A.quote: I don't want to chat with my capex decision. A friendly bot that writes fluent paragraphs is exactly what makes up numbers.

walkthrough: Day 0, 15 min: Wizard step 1 (6 company fields) is fine. Step 2: Problem category, and I hesitate between Operations and Finance because a plant decision is both. Step 3: the suggested KPIs are generic. I type NPV, IRR, payback and utilisation. Step 4: budget and constraints are fine. Saving as a draft is good.

Day 0, 5 min: The data page table has templates I can download. I like that, since my analyst can fill templates. STUCK #1: there's no obvious way to invite the analyst. I'd have to email the templates to him and upload them myself.
Day 1–4, 20 min of my time: I relay files between my analyst and the portal. That's annoying.
Day 4, 3 min: The dashboard shows 'Data 80%, Analysis 45%'. STUCK #2: 45% of what? Which of the missing 20% matters? It doesn't tell me what to do next. I email the consultant to ask.

Day 9, 40 min: The formal PDF has a methodology section and a confidence appendix, which my board recognises. SUSPICIOUS #3: confidence sits in an appendix, separate from each number, so I have to cross-reference. The approver approves the whole report in one click, so I don't know whether each finding was checked.
Day 10, 30 min: My analyst rebuilds the key numbers to verify them. The report is usable if they match.
C.quote: It looks like something my auditors would recognise, which helps. But '45% analysis progress' means nothing to me, and putting confidence in an appendix is where uncomfortable caveats get hidden.

interrogation.a: Finding a single number that I can't trace back to my data or to a stated assumption, presented as fact. Once I find one invented figure, I treat everything else as invented too, and I'm gone.
interrogation.b: Every number tagged with its source: the ERP file and field, a named external source, or 'ASSUMPTION' with who set it and why. An assumptions table I can edit, with the outputs recalculating. A sensitivity table, e.g. payback if demand is -15% or capex is +20%. Confidence per finding, not in an appendix. The alternatives compared side by side (extra shift, outsourcing, new plant). Confirmation that a named human consultant checked each finding. And an Excel export of the model so my analyst can audit it.
interrogation.c: In B: proper roles for my analyst (data access only, and nothing he sees in the report before I release it). A 'Sources & assumptions' panel attached to every finding, with click-through to the uploaded rows. Excel model export alongside PDF/Word. A visible line showing which datasets were used and which were ignored, and why.
interrogation.d: A 'decision scenarios' sandbox: I adjust the main drivers (demand growth, capex, utilisation, financing rate) and watch NPV/IRR and the recommendation change, with a 'break-even point' shown, i.e. the demand level at which the second plant stops making sense. Plus a 'challenge this number' button that forces the system either to show the source calculation or to admit it's an assumption. That's what would turn a skeptic like me into a user.
